stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: Rains shut Chhattisgarh schools; 13 MP districts on heavy rain alert
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Rains shut Chhattisgarh schools; 13 MP districts on heavy rain alert
stories.summary: Heavy rain has shut schools across Chhattisgarh and put riverside villages on flood alert, while the IMD has warned of very heavy rain in 13 Madhya Pradesh districts.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - Chhattisgarh has closed all government, private and aided schools on Saturday amid heavy rain and flooding concerns.
- Water releases from the Gangrel Dam have raised the alert for villages along the Mahanadi.
- The IMD has warned of very heavy rain in 13 Madhya Pradesh districts as a depression moves towards Uttar Pradesh.
Heavy rain has disrupted travel across parts of Chhattisgarh, prompting a statewide school holiday on Saturday and flood alerts for riverside villages.
In neighbouring Madhya Pradesh, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned of very heavy rain in 13 districts.
Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai ordered all government, private and aided schools to remain closed on 26 September.
He urged parents to keep children at home and directed district administrations to stay ready for relief and rescue work.
Rain has submerged roads and affected connections between districts, particularly in Bastar and adjoining areas.
In Mahasamund, rising water in the Mahanadi and releases from the Gangrel Dam have put 18 riverside villages on alert.
Two guards stranded by floodwater at a liquor shop in Bamhani village were rescued.
All 14 gates of the Gangrel Dam in Dhamtari have been opened as the reservoir filled following sustained rain.
The additional discharge has increased concern for settlements downstream.

stories.headline: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu orders urgent relief measures in flood-hit areas
stories.title: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu orders urgent relief measures in flood-hit areas
stories.summary: The Chief Minister directs officials to expedite the process of restoration of power supply, distribute 50 kg of rice to each fisherfolk family, and evolve plans to construct two barrages, one upstream and another downstream of Prakasam Barrage, to impound local floodwaters
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Saturday told the officials to expedite the process of restoration of power supply in the areas that received heavy rains due to the deep depression in the Bay of Bengal and to distribute 50 kg of rice free of cost to each one of the fisherfolk families who could not venture into the sea for the last five days.

Taking stock of the situation in a teleconference along with Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu and Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad and other senior officials, Mr. Naidu said Vamsadhara water should be diverted into the Hiramandalam reservoir to utilise the floodwaters to the extent possible.

He ordered that relief measures be taken urgently in the waterlogged areas and steps initiated to assess the loss incurred by the agriculture sector so that compensation could be paid with contribution from the Central government.

The Chief Minister ordered that reservoirs across the State be filled with rainwater and called for plans to construct two barrages, one upstream and one downstream of Prakasam Barrage, to impound the local floodwaters and they be sent to the Centre for approval.
The officials told Mr. Naidu that there were no inflows into the Krishna and the rise in water level at Prakasam Barrage was due to the local floods.
Officials explained that the overall rainfall deficit dropped from 50% to 31% due to recent rains.
Coastal Andhra had 19.80% deficit while Rayalaseema 42% deficit.
Though rains subsided for now, river inflows from upstream areas in North Andhra continued, they said.

stories.headline: Election Commission’s bid at damage control raises more questions
stories.title: Election Commission’s bid at damage control raises more questions
stories.summary: The Election Commission’s bid to project unity may have backfired: after all the three Commissioners met, its statement appeared to acknowledge lapses flagged by The Indian Express.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - All three Election Commissioners met on 26 September amid criticism of the Commission’s handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
- A press note issued after the meeting announced changes to meeting procedures, voter-registration requirements and the handling of some SIR cases.
- The measures address several issues raised in The Indian Express investigation, but questions remain about how earlier decisions were made.
The jury is out on whether the Election Commission of India on Saturday climbed out of the hole it dug for itself since June, 2025 or it merely succeeded in digging the hole deeper.

As protests spread across the country for removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, scrapping the contentious Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and an independent inquiry into the Commission’s functioning, all three Commissioners met at 3 pm on Saturday and tried to reassure people that all is well.
All is not well though.

Even as the Election Commission met today, a damning claim was made by a former Chief secretary of Kerala, Jiji Thomson, who claimed to Manorama Online that Gyanesh Kumar in 2016 had asked him to contest on a BJP ticket.
While Kumar was appointed an Election Commissioner in March, 2024 and became the Chief Election Commissioner in February, 2025, the damning claim reveals his close association with the ruling party.
It would make his position more untenable and make it more difficult for him to remain in his post.

The bland press note issued by the ECI, being described as too little and coming too late, showed both desperation and a desperate attempt to repair the damage done to the Commission’s image and credibility.

The press note issued today, 26 September 2026, does no deny any of the points raised in the Indian Express report and by two of the Election Commissioners on 14 different occasions in the last 10 months, as reported by the Express and others.
The press note in fact accepts that no agenda was being circulated before the meetings of the Commission and no minutes afterwards.

stories.headline: A ‘superior’ CEC renders Election Commissioners ‘non-functional’, Supreme Court had warned
stories.title: A ‘superior’ CEC renders Election Commissioners ‘non-functional’, Supreme Court had warned
stories.summary: Judgement stressed collegial functioning of poll panel and said ECs must have a say in decision-making
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Nearly four decades ago, the Supreme Court had warned that if a Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) functions in a way that he considers himself superior and his word final, the Election Commissioners (ECs) would be rendered “non-functional or ornamental”.
The court had held that leaving the “exclusive and uncontrolled” powers of the Election Commission of India (ECI) in the hands of one person would violate democratic rule.

The observations of the apex court in S.S. Dhanoa versus Union of India (1991), highlighting the importance of a collegial and multi-member ECI to democracy, still echo even as allegations of unilateral conduct, authoritarianism and subversion against CEC Gyanesh Kumar highlight friction within the poll panel.

A Constitution Bench in the T.N. Seshan case, which upheld a multi-member ECI, quoted the Dhanoa judgment’s reasoning that “vast discretionary powers, with virtually no checks and balances, should not be left in the hands of a single individual and it was desirable that more than one person should be associated with the exercise of such discretionary powers”.
The court had reasoned that a single and wise individual may be able to withstand all the pulls and pressures which many may not.
However, it is politic to entrust the affairs of the ECI with more than one hand for the sole reason that the institution is armed with vast powers and is accountable to none.

The spirit of the judgment is reflected in Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which requires the ECI to conduct its business unanimously or by the opinion of the majority consensus.
The court had said that the CEC must be able to conduct himself at meetings he chairs in a manner that he is able to win the confidence of his colleagues on the Commission and carry them with him.
On the other hand, this would prove difficult if the CEC, who is the chairman of a multi-member ECI, treats the other members of the Commission as his subordinates.
The T.N. Seshan judgment held that ECs were indeed a part of the Election Commission and “must have a say in decision-making”.
The court had at the time rejected an argument that the ECs’ role was restricted to merely tendering advice to the CEC.
The ECI is not the only multi-member body, the court had noted.

stories.headline: CPI leader Binoy Viswam demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged BJP ties
stories.title: CPI leader Binoy Viswam demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged BJP ties
stories.summary: This comes after former Kerala Chief Secretary Jiji Thomson claimed that Gyanesh Kumar urged him to contest Parliamentary elections on a BJP ticket in 2016.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar’s total subservience to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has been exposed fully, following the startling revelation by the former Chief Secretary, Jiji Thomson, the State secretary of CPI, Binoy Viswam has said.

Mr. Thomson had earlier alleged that during his tenure as the Chief Secretary, Mr. Kumar had once asked him why he did not contest Parliamentary elections on a BJP ticket, saying he could have become a Union Minister.
According to Mr. Thomson, the conversation had happened in 2016, while the two were travelling on the same flight to New Delhi.

In a statement here, Mr. Viswam said that by offering the lure of a Union Minister’s post under the BJP to a senior civil servant in Keralam, Mr. Kumar has proved that he is someone who is willing to stoop to any level for the BJP.
He said Mr. Kumar later headed the infamous Ayodhya Trust and that the BJP is using the same person to crush democracy for Amit Shah, Mr. Viswam added.
He alleged that Mr. Kumar had been made the CEC as a reward for all the intrigues he has carried out on behalf of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Shah.
Mr. Kumar’s conduct has now become unacceptable even to the other Election Commissioners, he stated.
Mr. Kumar has robbed 13 crore Indians of their right to vote and is a disgrace to the world’s largest democracy.
All democratic-minded Indians now believe that elections can never be free and fair under such an individual, Mr. Viswam claimed.
He demanded that Mr. Kumar should resign from the CEC post immediately if he retained even a shred of loyalty to the Constitution or that he would have to surrender before mounting public fury.
Mr. Viswam added that after Mr. Kumar’s exit, the Electronic Voting Machines too need to exit Indian democracy.

stories.headline: Election Commission holds crucial meeting amid SIR row, announces key decisions
stories.title: Election Commission holds crucial meeting amid SIR row, announces key decisions
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Saturday said all decisions taken on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, including the nationwide exercise, were approved unanimously, while announcing measures to simplify the process for voters facing notices over discrepancies.

The clarification comes amid row over report that claimed differences within the EC over SIR of electoral rolls." In the recent months, the Commission has taken numerous decisions including SIR across the country.
The order for the SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all the States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission.
The same has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India vide its order dated 27.5.2026.
The schedule for SIR for 12 States and UTs was issued on 27.10.2025 and those for 19 States/UTs was issued on 14.05.2026 with the unanimous approval of the Commission.
The final figure of number of electors will be known only after final publication in the remaining 12 states of Phase-III," the poll body said in a statement.

At a meeting held on Saturday, the Commission decided that voters who receive notices during the ongoing SIR over being unmapped or having logical discrepancies will not ordinarily have to appear before the electoral registration officer (ERO).
Booth-level officers (BLOs) will visit their homes to collect documents and upload them on ECINet for the ERO to decide.
Hearings will be held only in exceptional cases, preferably online.
An adult family member can also attend a hearing on behalf of the elector if authorised.
The Commission said facilities for online hearings would be strengthened.

The Commission also directed district election officers to set up help desks and special camps for people living in night shelters, labourers, poor people and homeless persons, depending on local requirements.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu among pronounced drought hotspots as South Peninsular India sees strongest drought trend: study
stories.title: Tamil Nadu among pronounced drought hotspots as South Peninsular India sees strongest drought trend: study
stories.summary: While less than 10% of the region was affected by drought in much of the period before the 1990s, several years after 2000 saw more than 40% of the region under drought conditions
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tamil Nadu is among the more pronounced drought hotspots in India, as a new 52-year analysis has found that South Peninsular India, the region that includes Tamil Nadu, recorded the strongest long-term increase in drought-affected area among the four broad climatic regions of the country.

The study, ‘Evolution of Climate Extremes Over the Indian Subcontinent Using a Revised CEI’, published in the International Journal of Climatology, analysed daily rainfall and temperature data from 1971 to 2022 to assess changes in multiple climate extremes.
The researchers developed a revised India Climate Extremes Index (IndCEI) combining seven indicators, including heat, drought, dry spells, and heavy rainfall.
The study found a strong positive trend in drought-affected areas over South Peninsular India, with the trend being the strongest among the four regions.
While less than 10% of the region was affected by drought in much of the period before the 1990s, several years after 2000 saw more than 40% of the region under drought conditions.
The researchers noted that severe and persistent drought conditions were particularly evident during the 2010s and early 2020s.
The study’s regional classification places Tamil Nadu within South Peninsular India.

A media note accompanying the research identifies Tamil Nadu, along with Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, among the eastern coastal States where the area affected by drought increased by 20% to 30% during 2011–2021, compared to the 1980s.
The researchers used the Standardised Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) to assess drought.
Unlike an indicator based only on rainfall, SPEI incorporates both precipitation and potential evapotranspiration, thereby capturing the influence of increasing temperatures on water availability.
The findings also point to a growing heat burden over southern India.
The area experiencing high maximum-temperature extremes has increased in South Peninsular India, particularly since the 2010s.

stories.headline: Deendayal Port Authority, Assam Petro-Chemicals lay foundation stone for ₹2,300-crore e-methanol plant in Gujarat
stories.title: Deendayal Port Authority, Assam Petro-Chemicals lay foundation stone for ₹2,300-crore e-methanol plant in Gujarat
stories.summary: The ₹2,300-crore project is aimed at supplying cleaner fuel to the maritime sector and is part of the port’s plan to develop itself as a green-fuel and bunkering hub
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: The Deendayal Port Authority (DPA) and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd (APCL) on Saturday laid the foundation stone for a 150 tonnes-per-day (TPD) e-methanol plant at Gandhidham, in a project estimated to cost ₹2,300 crore and expected to create more than 3,500 direct and indirect jobs.

The facility, being developed as a joint venture between DPA and APCL, is aimed at supplying cleaner fuel to the maritime sector and is part of Kandla’s larger plan to develop itself as a green-fuel and bunkering hub.

The foundation stone was laid at Gandhidham in the presence of Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, and Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal.
The project brings together APCL’s industrial capabilities with DPA’s port infrastructure.
The plant will produce 150 tonnes of e-methanol a day.
The project is expected to support the development of a wider ecosystem covering production, storage, handling and bunkering of green fuels at Kandla Port.
The project has evolved from an earlier proposal.
In January, DPA and APCL had signed an MoU for the 150-TPD facility, with the investment then pegged at ₹1,200 crore.
The latest announcement puts the project cost at about ₹2,300 crore.
The businessline had first reported about Kandla’s larger green-fuel plan in August 2025.

The plan was linked to the development of green shipping corridors and Kandla’s potential role as a low-carbon marine-fuel supply point.

opening: The Deendayal Port Authority (DPA) and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd (APCL) on Saturday laid the foundation stone for a 150 tonnes-per-day (TPD) e-methanol plant at Gandhidham, in a project estimated to cost ₹2,300 crore and expected to create more than 3,500 direct and indirect jobs.

The facility, being developed as a joint venture between DPA and APCL, is aimed at supplying cleaner fuel to the maritime sector and is part of Kandla’s larger plan to develop itself as a green-fuel and bunkering hub.
body: The foundation stone was laid at Gandhidham in the presence of Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, and Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal.
The project brings together APCL’s industrial capabilities with DPA’s port infrastructure.
The plant will produce 150 tonnes of e-methanol a day.
The project is expected to support the development of a wider ecosystem covering production, storage, handling and bunkering of green fuels at Kandla Port.
The project has evolved from an earlier proposal.
In January, DPA and APCL had signed an MoU for the 150-TPD facility, with the investment then pegged at ₹1,200 crore.
